name: IBM Brisbane backend governing the trial: 127 qubits — first quantum-hardware-in-the-loop clinical trial on the consciousness question (Cell, The Innovation 7(9):101355)
Multicenter trial: 13 hospitals across the UK and Spain — first large-scale randomized double-blind quantum consciousness trial
Survivors completing forced-choice recall + NDE scales: 142 — 47 group A entangled-natural, 49 group B entangled-neutral, 46 group C random-neutral
Stimulus delivery began 120 s after arrest onset; 10-qubit EM1/CM1 circuits on the backend; recall lucidity rose momentarily as NIRS dropped
Biomarker models explained up to 56.8% of recall variance (group A adjusted R² = 0.568); entangled groups A and B beat chance, control C at chance
Nonlocal perception predicted 32% of Greyson NDE-scale variance (SEM); expectation bias ruled out via overlap coefficient
Overlap coefficient between entangled groups A and B: 0.843 — above the 0.7 equivalence threshold (A-C 0.584, B-C 0.683 below)
Mermin-GHZ inequality values 368.7117 (A) and 347.6603 (B) — above the 23 entanglement threshold; 512 is the theoretical GHZ limit for 10 qubits
Fisher-Escolà Q: 0.4985 (A), 0.5212 (B) vs 0.459 critical at α=0.0001 — structured deviation from randomness; the paper itself says not direct evidence of quantum causation
Fabrication allegation: For Better Science 2026-09-22 calls the trial fabricated/papermill slop — UNADJUDICATED, pending +1 fuel; this seal encodes the reported numbers, not the claim's truth
